This page is the workshop's quick-reference index. For everything in detail, see the [Syllabus](Syllabus.qmd) and [Schedule](Schedule.qmd).

The workshop's lectures, tutorials, datasets, and reference material live on this Quarto-built website. The source is on GitHub at <https://github.com/wcresko/scRNAseq_tutorial> — pull requests and issues welcome.

## How to use this site

- The **navbar** at the top is the primary navigation. The **search** icon (magnifying glass) finds anything across the site.
- Lectures are revealjs **slides** — open in a browser, use arrow keys to advance.
- Tutorials are **Quarto** (`.qmd`) source files — download and open in RStudio.
- Most pages have a **left-side TOC** that scrolls with you and a **back-to-top** link in the footer.
- The site supports a **light/dark theme** toggle in the top-right of every page; both meet WCAG AA contrast.

## Technical requirements

- A laptop with at least 16 GB RAM and \~10 GB free disk
- R ≥ 4.4 ([install here](https://www.r-project.org)) and RStudio Desktop ([install here](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/))
- A terminal with `ssh` (only needed for Talapas-track tutorials)
- A GitHub account (for cloning the repo and following the version-control workflow in [Appendix E](Resources_Folder/Appendix_E_Git_GitHub.html))
- Reliable internet for the first install (\~5 GB of packages); after that, all tutorials run offline

The full setup is in the [Setup](Setup.qmd) page — run that before Day 1.

## Acknowledgments

The hands-on tutorials build on:

- **Khushbu Patel's** [YouTube Tutorials repo](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials) (DESeq2 primer, scATAC-seq, WGCNA worked examples)
- **The Satija lab's** [Seurat tutorials](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/) (PBMC 3k, integration, spatial)
- **The Sengupta lab's** [scNotebooks](https://integrativebioinformatics.github.io/scNotebooks/) — the LatinCells / Human Cell Atlas / Wellcome Connecting Sciences curriculum we cross-reference throughout

The reproducibility infrastructure (renv, Apptainer / Docker images, CI smoke tests) draws on the patterns documented in the [Bioconductor Workshop Galaxy](https://workshop.bioconductor.org/) and the [Carpentries](https://carpentries.org/) lesson-development guides.
